items.name: Library browser (floating tab groups)
items.description: Two-pane browser of any item set with multi-select and Compare: each selection opens as a tab in a floating group with undock, drag-and-drop, split (vertical/horizontal/four-way/grid), minimize to corners or a floating toolbar, tree/grid element explorer. Attaches to the tab groups an app declares in axf.manifest.json → libraries.browser.tabGroups.

params.label: Tab groups to attach to
params.help: Ids of the tab groups this browser binds to; each gets a route and a Compare command.

params.label: Item kinds
params.help: Tab kinds the browser may open; each kind needs a registered TabRenderer.

params.label: Toolbar on new windows
params.help: forced = window schema rules; element windows start off.

items.name: axHub connector (first slice: approvals feed, hub address, locked web view)
items.description: What axHub serves today, for any AXF app: hub address rules (https host only; links checked against that exact origin), hub URLs (approvals, one approval by id, sign-in, account, app catalog), the approvals feed GET /auth/admin/approvals.json (axHub decision #85) read with the app's own hub session (web: the browser's cookie, credentials included; Android: the WebView cookie store) with redirects refused and the reply size-capped, mapped to ok / signed-out / not-admin / unreachable, seen-id tracking so each approval rings once, sign-out on the hub (CSRF form post), and on Android a web view locked to one origin plus hub APK downloads through the download manager. Web (framework/libs/hub) and Kotlin (lib-hub HubRules) replay one fixture, spec/fixtures/hub-approvals.json. The hub protocol contract (AXPP) is a named placeholder, parked for Fable.

android.note: written without a compiler; CI compiles and runs :lib-hub:testDebugUnitTest (HubRules replayed the fixture with a local kotlinc)

placeholders.note: The hub protocol contract (AXPP): typed calls, jobs and events between an AXF app and axHub. Parked for Fable; not designed here.
Hub-pushed approvals and events instead of polling the feed.
The hub's admin API (services, jobs, audit, vault names, users, projects), hub step 4.

items.name: App lock (fingerprint/face or PIN)
items.description: Second-step unlock any app can put after its own first step: strong biometrics through BiometricPrompt, or a 4–12 digit PIN kept only as a salted PBKDF2 hash in the Keystore-backed secure store. Failed PINs lock out with a doubling delay. Settings group App lock (mode, auto-lock delay) and a set/change PIN screen (current PIN required to change). Fills the platform's android.biometric placeholder.

placeholders.note: Keystore keys that need the fingerprint for every decrypt (CryptoObject). Not built: the lock gates the UI; data keys don't require auth yet.

items.name: MCP client (connect to MCP servers)
items.description: Any AXF app as an MCP client: a server registry (records in the key-value store, tokens only in the platform secure store), Streamable HTTP sessions (JSON-RPC, SSE replies, session ids, version negotiation, pagination, cancellation, timeouts), browsing tools/resources/prompts and calling tools under the kernel interop exposure rules (mcp.call / mcp.call.write / mcp.call.destructive + confirmation). Pure-Kotlin engine in the kernel (ai.amberx.axf.kernel.mcp) mirrors framework/core/engines/mcp.ts and framework/python/axf_libs/mcp; all three replay spec/fixtures/mcp-client.json. Registers the kernel's axf.remote (RemoteServices) provider.

android.note: written without a compiler; CI compiles and runs :lib-mcp:testDebugUnitTest

placeholders.note: MCP server side (expose the app's surface@1 actions as tools) — not built; the client half is this library.
OAuth 2.1 authorization-code sign-in to MCP servers — not built; bearer tokens only.
Server→client requests (sampling, elicitation) are ignored, not answered.

items.name: Notifications (channels, private lock-screen alerts)
items.description: Android notifications with the privacy rules built in: channels (importance, lock-screen visibility, vibration, badge), canPost (POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+; every post checks it), canFullScreen (Android 14+ per-app opt-in), the quiet ongoing "watching" notification for a foreground service, high-priority alerts that are VISIBILITY_PRIVATE with a public version (the lock screen shows only e.g. "Approval waiting"), full screen only when asked and allowed, quiet notices, post/cancel by tag or id. Never shows the app over the lock screen. Hook for alert@1 deliveries (AlertNotifications.plan / AxfNotifications.deliverAlert, channel "device"). Fills the platform's android.notifications placeholder.

android.note: written without a compiler; CI compiles and runs :lib-notifications:testDebugUnitTest

placeholders.note: alert@1 deliveries posted as device notifications; the hook exists (AxfNotifications.deliverAlert), nothing subscribes AlertCenter yet.
Scheduled notifications (with the work scheduler, x.work).

items.name: Voice (speech in, prompts out, voice commands)
items.description: One-shot speech recognition as a suspend call (on-device recognizer for secret speech when the phone has one), spoken prompts that finish before the next listen, and an open registry of voice commands. Every command ships default trigger phrases; users switch defaults off, record their own (pick from what the recognizer heard) or type them in Settings → Voice triggers. Pure-Kotlin phrase matching (normalize, fuzzy trigger + label scores) so other ports can mirror it.

params.label: Prefer on-device recognition
params.help: Secret speech (passwords) always uses the on-device recognizer when the phone has one.

placeholders.note: Always-on wake word in a foreground service (not built; the app listens only while open).

items.name: Work (poll jobs in a foreground service, boot restart)
items.description: The Android host for work@1 poll jobs: an app registers a job (a kernel JobSpec: interval bounds as data, one rule per outcome with fixed / exponential / interval delays, one-time notices per spell, run conditions read from the app's own prefs, foreground + boot restart) whose body is a suspend function that only calls libraries; the loop is the framework's. PollService (foreground, specialUse) drives every job through the kernel's WorkEngine state machine and only carries out its effects (run, sleep, stop, notice, status); START / CHECK_NOW / STOP / INTERVAL commands; a refused foreground start stops quietly; START_STICKY; WorkBootReceiver restarts jobs after a reboot or update when their conditions hold; running-state + state flows per job; the ongoing notification through lib-notifications, rebuilt from the job's state after every run. Fills the platform's android.work placeholder. The engine is cross-port: framework/core/engines/work.ts = ai.amberx.axf.kernel.work.WorkEngine, fixture spec/fixtures/work.json.

android.note: written without a compiler; CI compiles and runs :lib-work:testDebugUnitTest (the kernel engine + WorkConformanceTest and JobRunner were compiled and replayed with a local kotlinc)

web.note: engine + reducer only (no timer host yet); self-test spec/check-work.mts

placeholders.note: The kernel's WorkScheduler contract (axf.work) on WorkManager: constrained periodic work, 15 min minimum, survives process death.
